name: one-ml
desc: Reboot of ML, unifying its core and (now first-class) module layers
why: Research ML dialect unifying modules and core types; an obscure language with a genuinely unusual design pedigree from Rossberg's work.

brief.what_it_is: 1ML is an experimental reboot of the ML functional language in which modules are first-class values and the core language and the module layer are merged into one small language. The homepage describes it as a language where functions, functors, and type constructors are one construct, and structures, records, and tuples are not distinguished. The homepage links a simple prototype interpreter, version 0.1, which runs small examples. It is a research artifact rather than a production tool. The homepage does not say what input or output format the interpreter uses beyond running ML-style programs.
brief.why_it_exists: ML splits into a core language of types and expressions and a separate higher-order module language, which duplicates syntax and semantics and limits expressiveness, for example by preventing a module from being selected by a dynamic decision. The author's framing is that 1ML is a redesign that makes modules truly first-class and unifies the two layers into one language.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives the design at a high level: 1ML does not require dependent types, and its type structure can be expressed in plain System Fω (a variant of the F-ing modules approach). The author describes it either as one language where everything is a mode of use of modules, or as a user-friendly surface syntax for System Fω. The homepage does not explain the interpreter's internals.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says you need OCaml 4.02 and Make to build the prototype, and that the README in the GitHub repository has basic documentation. I did not fetch the repository, so I have no build or run commands. The Homebrew formula lists an executable named 1ml, which suggests the interpreter is installed under that name.
brief.standout: It is a design-research language arguing that the core/module split in ML is unnecessary, and that functions, functors, type constructors, structures, and records can be one construct. It also claims the type system fits in plain System Fω without dependent types, and that it can be presented with Damas/Milner-style implicit quantification.
brief.status: Unknown from the homepage alone. The page has a copyright line of 2015-2017, and the prototype is listed as Version 0.1, with no release date or last-commit date shown. The papers are from 2015 to 2018. The page does not mention recent activity, and the GitHub repository was not fetched.
brief.caveats: The prototype is a simple interpreter that does not yet implement the effect polymorphism extension from the latest paper. The author states that type inference for the implicitly typed version is not complete, though he argues it is not substantially worse than Standard ML's. It needs OCaml 4.02 and Make to build, which is an old OCaml version. The homepage describes the project as research, and the scout notes call it obscure.
quotes: 1ML is a reboot of ML starting from first-class modules, and unifies core and module layer into one small and consistent language.
In this "1ML", functions, functors, and even type constructors are one and the same construct; likewise, no distinction is made between structures, records, or tuples.
Yet, 1ML does not require dependent types, and its type structure is expressible in terms of plain System Fω, in a minor variation of our F-ing modules approach.
fetch_log: https://people.mpi-sws.org/~rossberg/1ml/ : fetched OK. Homepage text only; lists the ICFP 2015, extended 2015, JFP 2018, and WadlerFest 2016 papers without URLs, and a GitHub repository link with no URL in the text. I did not follow the GitHub link, so the README was not read.
